rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains Yahya's name by saying God gave him life through faith.
rows.anchor: قتادة: سماه الله يحيى لأنه أحياه بالإيمان

rows.speaker: الحسن بن المفضل
rows.claim: Al-Hasan ibn al-Mufaddal says Yahya was alive through protection from sin and obedience.
rows.anchor: الحسن بن المفضل: حي بالعصمة والطاعة

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم بن حبيب
rows.claim: Abu al-Qasim ibn Habib connects the name to Yahya's martyrdom, since martyrs are alive.
rows.anchor: أبو القاسم بن حبيب: سمي يحيى لأنه استشهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the world's low standing before God is shown by a woman killing Yahya ibn Zakariya.
rows.anchor: من هوان الدنيا على الله أن يحيى بن زكريا قتلته امرأة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil says Yahya was named because God brought him to life between an old man and an old woman.
rows.anchor: مقاتل: سمي يحيى لأنه أحياه بين شيخ وعجوز

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Yahya lived through the knowledge and wisdom granted to him.
rows.anchor: الزجاج: حي بالعلم والحكمة التي أوتيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God revived Yahya's mother's barrenness through him.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: إن الله أحيا به عقر أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes Yahya to mean that he will die, a hopeful naming like al-mafaza and al-salim.
rows.anchor: معناه يموت فسمي يحيى تفاؤلا، كالمفازة والسليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says God gave people life through Yahya by guiding them.
rows.anchor: لأن الله أحيا به الناس بالهدى

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority, including Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Hasan, Qatada, and Suddi, take God's word to be Jesus.
rows.anchor: الجمهور على أن الكلمة هو عيسى، وسيأتي لم سمي كلمة، قاله ابن عباس، ومجاهد

rows.speaker: الربيع وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Rabi and others say Yahya was the first to affirm Jesus and testify that he was God's word.
rows.anchor: الربيع، وغيره: كان يحيى أول من صدق بعيسى وشهد أنه كلمة من الله

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most say Yahya was six months older than Jesus; another view makes the difference three years, and Yahya died before Jesus was raised.
rows.anchor: وكان يحيى أكبر من عيسى بستة أشهر، قاله الأكثرون وقيل: بثلاث سنين، وقتل قبل رفع عيسى

rows.speaker: الربيع وغيره
rows.claim: Yahya's mother said her unborn child moved, bowed, or nodded toward Mary's unborn child, which was his first confirmation of Jesus.
rows.anchor: أم يحيى تقول لمريم: إني لأجد الذي في بطني يتحرك، وفي رواية: يسجد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وغيره
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and others read God's word as scripture, such as the Torah and Gospel; the singular is generic and can stand for a plural.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة، وغيره بكلمة من الله أي: بكتاب من الله التوراة والإنجيل وغيرهما، أوقع المفرد موقع الجمع

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: The Arabs call a poem a word; when Hudayra was mentioned, Hassan used kalimatuhu to mean his poem.
rows.anchor: الحويدرة ذكر لحسان، فقال: لعن الله كلمته، أي قصيدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith calls Labid's couplet the truest words spoken by a poet, illustrating that kalima can mean a poem.
rows.anchor: أصدق كلمة قالها شاعر كلمة لبيد: ألا كل شيء ما خلا الله باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation understands the word here as God's promise.
rows.anchor: معنى: بكلمة من الله هنا أي: بوعد من الله

rows.speaker: أبو السمال العدوي
rows.claim: Abu al-Simal al-Adawi reads kalima with kasra on kaf and a still lam throughout the Quran, a sound dialect that avoids two successive kasras; some also still the lam after fatḥa because of the kasra's weight.
rows.anchor: أبو السمال العدوي: بكلمة، بكسر الكاف وسكون اللام في جميع القرآن، وهي لغة فصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Musaddiqan is a circumstantial accusative; Ibn Atiyya calls it emphatic given the state of these prophets.
rows.anchor: مصدقا، على الحال. قال ابن عطية: وهي حال مؤكدة بحسب حال هؤلاء الأنبياء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas defines sayyid as noble or generous in rank.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: السيد الكريم. وقال قتادة: الحليم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada defines sayyid as forbearing, illustrated by a verse about one whose forbearance survives the ignorant.
rows.anchor: قتادة: الحليم، ومنه قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima defines a master as one not overcome by anger.
rows.anchor: عكرمة: من لا يغلبه الغضب. وقال الضحاك: الحسن الخلق

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak defines sayyid as one of good character.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: الحسن الخلق. وقال سالم: التقي

rows.speaker: سالم
rows.claim: Salim defines sayyid as Godfearing.
rows.anchor: سالم: التقي. وقال ابن زيد: الشريف

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd defines sayyid as distinguished or noble.
rows.anchor: ابن زيد: الشريف. وقال ابن المسيب: الفقيه العالم

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib defines sayyid as a learned jurist.
rows.anchor: ابن المسيب: الفقيه العالم. وقال أحمد بن عاصم: الراضي بقضاء الله

rows.speaker: أحمد بن عاصم
rows.claim: Ahmad ibn Asim defines sayyid as one content with God's decree.
rows.anchor: أحمد بن عاصم: الراضي بقضاء الله. وقال الخليل: المطاع الفائق أقرانه

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil defines sayyid as one obeyed who surpasses his peers.
rows.anchor: الخليل: المطاع الفائق أقرانه. وقال أبو بكر الوراق: المتوكل

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq defines sayyid as one who relies on God.
rows.anchor: أبو بكر الوراق: المتوكل. وقال الترمذي: العظيم الهمة

rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi defines sayyid as a person of lofty aspiration.
rows.anchor: الترمذي: العظيم الهمة. وقال الثوري: السيد من لا يحسد

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawri defines a master as one who is not envied, playing on the saying that the envious cannot become masters.
rows.anchor: الثوري: السيد من لا يحسد من قولهم: الحسود لا يسود

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq defines sayyid as one who excels his people in goodness.
rows.anchor: أبو إسحاق: السيد الذي يفوق في الخير قومه

rows.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Some linguists define sayyid as a master whose obedience is due.
rows.anchor: بعض أهل اللغة: السيد المالك الذي تجب طاعته. ولهذا قيل للزوج: سيد

rows.speaker: سلمة عن الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra, as transmitted by Salama, gives sayyid the senses owner, chief, wise person, and generous person.
rows.anchor: سلمة عن الفراء: السيد المالك، والسيد الرئيس، والسيد الحكيم، والسيد السخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith praises the master who is given wealth and generosity, brings the poor near, and rarely complains about people; the same ideal gives generously and restrains harm.
rows.anchor: «السيد من أعطي مالا ورزق سماحا، فأدنى الفقراء، وقلت شكايته في الناس»

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Banu Salima called the miserly Jad ibn Qays their master, the Prophet objected and named Amr ibn al-Jamuh instead.
rows.anchor: فقالوا الجد بن قيس على بخله فقال عليه السلام: «وأي داء أدوى من البخل؟ سيدكم عمرو بن الجموح»

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet called Saad ibn Muadh their master, meaning their leader and the person they obeyed.
rows.anchor:
«قوموا إلى سيدكم» .
أي رئيسكم والمطاع فيكم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet called Hasan ibn Ali a master and said God might reconcile two great Muslim factions through him.
rows.anchor: «إن ابني هذا سيد، ولعل الله يصلح به بين فئتين عظيمتين من المسلمين»

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari defines sayyid as one who surpasses his people in honor and says Yahya never committed a sin, making him master of his people and all people.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري: السيد الذي يسود قومه أي يفوقها في الشرف. وكان يحيى قائما لقومه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya defines mastery as seeking people's satisfaction by noble means without wrongdoing: generosity, restraint from harming others, and forbearance through grave burdens.
rows.anchor: ابن عطية ما ملخصه: خصه الله بذكر السؤدد، وهو الاعتمال في رضا الناس على أشرف الوجوه دون أن يوقع في باطل

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya adds that mastery includes paying debts, repairing what is broken, rescuing people from danger, and may describe someone who falls short in recommended deeds but stands firm for rights without fearing blame.
rows.anchor: وتفصيله: بذل الندى وهو الكرم، وكف الأذى وهي العفة في الفرج واليد واللسان، واحتمال العظائم

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar said he had seen no greater master than Muawiya; he clarified that Abu Bakr and Umar were better, while Muawiya was more masterful.
rows.anchor: ابن عمر: ما رأيت أسود من معاوية؟ قيل له: وأبو بكر وعمر؟ قال: هما خير منه، ومعاوية أسود منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says all the reported definitions suit Yahya, since prophets are the people most deserving of perfected qualities.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأقوال التي ذكرت في تفسير السيد كلها يصلح أن يكون تفسيرا في وصف يحيى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sayyid is a laudatory title for anyone with mastery, but should not be applied to a wrongdoer, hypocrite, or unbeliever; the phrase about obeying masters reflects their own belief and claim.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: وسيدا، دلالة على إطلاق هذا الاسم على من فيه سيادة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report forbids calling a hypocrite a master; another says the Prophet told Banu Amir that God is the Master and they should speak normally.
rows.anchor: «لا تقولوا للمنافق سيدا» ، وما جاء من قوله أطعنا سادتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan explains the Prophet's answer to Banu Amir as a response to their affected flattery, or as predating his knowledge that he was master of humankind; he himself called Hasan, Saad, and Amr masters.
rows.anchor: فمحمول على أنه رآهم متكلفين لذلك، أو كان ذلك قبل أن يعلم أنه سيد البشر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وابن جبير وقتادة وعطاء وأبو الشعثاء والحسن والسدي وابن زيد
rows.claim: These authorities define hasur as a man who refrains from women despite having the ability to marry.
rows.anchor: وحصورا هو الذي لا يأتي النساء مع القدرة على ذلك، قاله ابن مسعود، وابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line glosses hasur as one who does not desire marriage or women.
rows.anchor: لا ولا يبتغي النساء الصباحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Yahya nevertheless married, to better restrain his gaze.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أنه تزوج مع ذلك ليكون أغض لبصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations make hasur someone who restrains himself from pleasures, from God's sins, or someone timid and awe inspiring.
rows.anchor: الحاصر نفسه عن الشهوات

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس والضحاك والمسيب
rows.claim: Another view from Ibn Masud, Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, and al-Musayyib takes hasur to mean impotent, unable to have intercourse or ejaculate.
rows.anchor: ابن مسعود أيضا، وابن عباس أيضا، والضحاك، والمسيب: هو العنين الذي لا ذكر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because hasur is praised here, Abu Hayyan takes it as acquired restraint rather than an inborn defect: Yahya held back from worldly desires, including women; their law may have treated abstention from women as asceticism.
rows.anchor: وإيراد الحصور وصفا في معرض الثناء الجميل إنما يكون عن الفعل المكتسب دون الجبلة في الغالب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid describes Yahya as eating plants and weeping from fear of God until his tears made a channel down his face.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: كان طعام يحيى العشب، وكان يبكي من خشية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation infers that a person in Yahya's condition would be occupied away from women and other worldly desires.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا حاله فهو في شغل عن النساء وغيرهن من شهوات الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another usage makes hasur someone who does not join people in gambling; al-Akhtal's verse illustrates the sense of abstaining from play and amusement.
rows.anchor: الحصور الذي لا يدخل مع القوم في الميسر. قال الأخطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when boys invited Yahya to play, he answered that he had not been created for play.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أنه: مر وهو طفل بصبيان فدعوه إلى اللعب، فقال: ما للعب خلقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usage of hasur and hasr can also mean one who keeps a secret, as in Jarir's line about guarding Umayma's secret.
rows.anchor: والحصور والحصر كما تم السر. قال جرير: ولقد تشاقطني الوشاة فصادفوا

rows.speaker: ابن العاصي
rows.claim: A report from Ibn al-Asi says Yahya lacked a man's sexual organ except for something like a little stick.
rows.anchor: الحديث عن ابن العاصي، ما معناه: أن يحيى لم يكن له ما للرجل إلا مثل هذا العود

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra likens Yahya's sexual organ to a tiny speck taken from the ground.
rows.anchor: رواية أبي هريرة: كان ذكره مثل هذه القذاة، يشير إلى قذاة من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term hasur has been used to argue that celibacy for voluntary worship is better than marriage; this is the majority position, while Abu Hanifa holds the reverse.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل بقوله وحصورا من ذهب إلى أن التبتل لنوافل العبادات أفضل من الاشتغال بالنكاح

words: مصدقا بكلمة من الله وسيدا وحصورا ونبيا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence moves from faith, to leadership among one's people, to asceticism from the especially difficult desire for women, and finally to the highest rank, prophethood.
rows.anchor: فذكر أولا الوصف الذي تبنى عليه الأوصاف بعده، وهو: التصديق الذي هو الإيمان، ثم ذكر السيادة

words: مصدقا بكلمة من الله وسيدا وحصورا ونبيا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan links Yahya's qualities to Mary's: both affirmed the truth, were called masters, abstained from sexual relations, and were associated with angelic speech and prophethood; Mary's extraordinary gifts prompted Zachariah's prayer for good offspring, answered with Yahya.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الأوصاف تشابه من أوصاف مريم عليها السلام، وذلك أن زكريا لما رأى ما اشتملت عليه مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Zachariah asked whether the promised child would be his own son or come through his descendants.
rows.anchor: الثاني: أنه لما بشر بالولد استعلم: أيكون ذلك الولد من صلبه نفسه أم من بينه

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: One view says Zachariah had forgotten his earlier request; forty years passed before the glad tidings, while Sufyan gives sixty years.
rows.anchor: الثالث: أنه كان نسي السؤال، وكان بين السؤال والتبشير أربعون سنة. ونقل عن سفيان أنه كان بينهما ستون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation treats the question as amazement at God's power on seeing signs, or as joy so great that Zachariah was dazed by an ordinarily unlikely event.
rows.anchor: الرابع: أن هذا الاستعلام هو على سبيل الاستعظام لقدرة الله تعالى، يحدث ذلك عند معاينة الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says his old age left him unable to have intercourse, so he asked whether God would strengthen him and enable his wife to conceive.
rows.anchor: الخامس: إنما سأل لأنه كان عاجزا عن الجماع لكبر سنه، فسأل ربه: هل يقويه على الجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says he asked whether the child would come from his barren wife or from another woman.
rows.anchor: السادس: سأل هل يرزق الولد من امرأته العاقر أم من غيرها

rows.speaker: عكرمة والسدي
rows.claim: Ikrima and al-Suddi report that Satan tried to spoil the glad tidings by suggesting the caller was Satan rather than the angels; Zachariah asked how he could have a son until revelation clarified it.
rows.anchor: فقال: أنى يكون لي غلام ليبين الله له من الوحي، قاله عكرمة، والسدي

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qadi rejects the Satan report's implication: if messengers could confuse an angel's speech with Satan's, trust in all revealed laws would collapse.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي: لو اشتبه على الرسل كلام الملك بكلام الشيطان لم يبق الوثوق بجميع الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A response says the Qadi's objection need not follow, since miracles may authenticate revelation about religion without confirming matters of worldly benefit, leaving uncertainty to be removed by inquiry.
rows.anchor: وأجيب: بأن ما قاله لا يلزم لاحتمال أن تقوم المعجزة على الوحي بما يتعلق بالدين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes the question as customary improbability, like Mary's question.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري: استبعاد من حيث العادة. كما قالت مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects al-Zamakhshari's reading: if Zachariah thought a child impossible by custom, he would not have prayed for offspring, especially as prophets often witness miracles.
rows.anchor: لو كان استبعادا لما سأله بقوله: هب لي من لدنك ذرية طيبة لأنه لا يسأل إلا ما كان ممكنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yakunu may be complete, with ghulam as subject, or incomplete; if incomplete, li need not be fronted over the noun because an interrogative licenses an indefinite subject, as can.
rows.anchor: و: يكون، يجوز أن تكون تامة وفاعلها غلام، أي: أنى يحدث لي غلام؟ ويجوز أن تكون ناقصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two following clauses are circumstantial; their governor is yakunu if complete, or li if it is incomplete.
rows.anchor: والجملتان بعد كل منهما حال، والعامل فيهما: يكون، إن كانت تامة، أو العامل في: لي، إن كانت ناقصة

rows.speaker: جبير بن نفير
rows.claim: Jubayr ibn Nufayr says Zachariah's tongue swelled inside his mouth until it filled it, then God released it after three days.
rows.anchor: جبير بن نفير: ربا لسانه في فيه حتى ملأه، ثم أطلقه الله بعد ثلاث

rows.speaker: الربيع وغيره
rows.claim: Al-Rabi and others say God restrained Zachariah's tongue as punishment for asking for a sign after angels had directly announced the glad tidings.
rows.anchor: الربيع، وغيره: أخذ الله عليه لسانه فجعل لا يقدر على الكلام معاقبة على سؤال آية

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari and a view also transmitted from Muhammad ibn Kab say there was no physical affliction: Zachariah could remember God but was prevented from ordinary conversation, freeing him to give thanks for the gift.
rows.anchor: قاله الطبري، وذكر نحوه عن محمد بن كعب، وكانت الآية حبس اللسان لتخلص المدة لذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan prefers an answer derived directly from the request: Zachariah could remember God but not speak to people despite a sound body, and conception occurred as foretold; the contrast itself was miraculous.
rows.anchor: وأحسن الجواب وأوقعه ما كان مشتقا من السؤال، ومنتزعا منه وكان الإعجاز في هذه الآية من جهة قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says Zachariah was ordered to fast for three days, during which people did not speak.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أمر أن يصوم ثلاثة أيام، وكانوا لا يتكلمون في صومهم

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abu Muslim suggests the sign was an order to stop speaking to people and devote himself to remembrance in thanks; Zachariah may have asked for a duty that would make the gift a cause for gratitude.
rows.anchor: أبو مسلم: يحتمل أن يكون معناه: آيتك أن تصير مأمورا بأن لا تكلم الخلق

words: ألا تكلم الناس ثلاثة أيام إلا رمزا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is that Zachariah asked for a sign of the birth: he could not speak to people for three days except by gesture, and was told to remember and glorify God; the silence could be voluntary, linked to their fasting law, or coercive, with or without physical affliction.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل عليه ظاهر الآية أنه سأل آية تدل على أنه يولد له، فأجابه بأن آيته انتفاء الكلام منه مع الناس

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the command to remember God refers to the days when Zachariah could not speak to people and was one of the striking signs.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري: ولذلك قال: واذكر ربك إلى آخره يعني في أيام عجزك عن تكليم الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says al-Zamakhshari's restriction is not necessary: the command may not be limited to the silence period, and remembrance need not mean spoken words.
rows.anchor: ولا يتعين ما قاله لما ذكرناه من احتمالات وجوه الانتفاء، ولأن الأمر بالذكر والتسبيح ليس مقيدا بالزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jaala means make or render and takes two objects: ayatan and li; li must be advanced because before jaala it licensed an indefinite subject.
rows.anchor: وظاهر: اجعل، هنا أنها بمعنى صير، فتتعدى لمفعولين: الأول آية، والثاني المجرور، قبله وهو: لي

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads an la tukallim with nominative mīm, treating an as a lightened inna with omitted subject pronoun, or as a source particle like ma.
rows.anchor: ابن أبي عبلة: أن لا تكلم، برفع الميم على أن: أن، هي المخففة من الثقيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan treats three days as a temporal adverbial; Kufans instead treat it as an object because the silence lasted through every part of the period.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب: ثلاثة أيام، على الظرف خلافا للكوفيين، إذ زعموا أنه كان اسم الزمان يستغرقه الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three days include their nights, as the parallel wording in Maryam says three nights; this weakens the interpretation that Zachariah was commanded to fast, since fasting nights is unlikely.
rows.anchor: والمراد: ثلاثة أيام بلياليها، يدل على ذلك قوله في سورة مريم: قال آيتك ألا تكلم الناس ثلاث ليال سويا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The starting time is unspecified: if the silence was voluntary, Zachariah could choose when to abstain or it may start with the address; if coercive, it apparently began at once.
rows.anchor: ولم يعين ابتداء ثلاثة أيام، بل أطلق فقال: ثلاثة أيام، فإن كان ذلك بتكليف فيمكن أن يكون ذلك موكولا إلى اختياره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer Quranic abrogation by Sunna if Zachariah could speak during the three days, his law bound Muslims, and the Prophet's prohibition of silence through night abrogated it.
rows.anchor: قيل: وفي ذلك دلالة على نسخ القرآن بالسنة، وهذا على تقدير قدرة زكريا على الكلام في تلك الأيام الثلاثة

rows.speaker: كثير من العلماء
rows.claim: Many scholars interpret the hadith against a day's silence as forbidding silence from remembering God; refraining from useless talk is good.
rows.anchor: كثير من العلماء إلى أن معناه: لا صمت يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some call the exception disconnected because gesture is not speech; it can be connected if speech also means signaling what is in the speaker's mind, as shown in Arabic poetry.
rows.anchor: واستثناء الرمز، قيل: هو استثناء منقطع، إذ الرمز لا يدخل تحت التكليم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari starts with a connected exception: a gesture performs what speech does and conveys the same understanding, so it can be called speech.
rows.anchor: الزمخشري. قال: لما أدى مؤدي الكلام، وفهم منه ما يفهم منه، سمي كلاما

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya chooses a disconnected exception because the verse means tongue speech, though gestures count as speech in legal contexts such as vows, making a connected reading possible there.
rows.anchor: ابن عطية فاختار أن يكون منقطعا. قال: والكلام المراد به في الآية إنما هو النطق باللسان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says ramz is moving the lips.
rows.anchor: الرمز هنا: تحريك بالشفتين، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: الضحاك والسدي وعبد الله بن كثير
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Abdullah ibn Kathir say ramz is a gesture with the hand and head.
rows.anchor: قاله الضحاك، والسدي، وعبد الله بن كثير

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan defines ramz as a hand gesture.
rows.anchor: إشارة باليد، قاله الحسن. أو: إيماء، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada defines ramz as a gesture, without specifying its form; another report from him says hand or eye gestures, also related from al-Hasan.
rows.anchor: إيماء، قاله قتادة. فالإيماء هو الإشارة لكنه لم يعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other definitions of ramz are writing on the ground, pointing with the index finger, using the tongue, or making a faint sound.
rows.anchor: وقيل: رمزه الكتابة على الأرض. وقيل: الإشارة بالإصبع المسبحة. وقيل: باللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line uses ramz for signaling words without being mute, illustrating the term's range.
rows.anchor: قول الشاعر: ظل أياما له من دهره ... يرمز الأقوال من غير خرس

rows.speaker: علقمة بن قيس ويحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Alqama ibn Qays and Yahya ibn Waththab read rumuzan with damma on both consonants, analyzed either as plural rumuz or as a verbal noun on fuul by vowel assimilation.
rows.anchor: علقمة بن قيس، ويحيى بن وثاب: رمزا، بضم الراء والميم، وخرج على أنه جمع رموز

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Amash reads ramazan with fatḥa on both consonants, as the plural of ramiz; in that analysis it is an accusative circumstantial phrase for the subject or people being addressed.
rows.anchor: الأعمش: رمزا، بفتح الراء والميم، وخرج على أنه جمع رامز، كخادم وخدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception supports treating gesture as a kind of speech, a principle found in much of the Sunna and accepted by the majority of jurists.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: إلا رمزا دلالة على أن الإشارة تتنزل منزلة الكلام، وذلك موجود في كثير من السنة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked where God was, a slave woman pointed toward heaven; the Prophet ordered that she be freed because she was a believer, accepting a gesture as evidence of faith.
rows.anchor: «أين الله» . فأشارت برأسها إلى السماء، فقال: «أعتقها فإنها مؤمنة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this gesture established faith, the foundation that protects life and property and leads to paradise, Abu Hayyan says signs can serve across religions; this is the majority jurists' view.
rows.anchor: فأجاز الإسلام بالإشارة وهو أصل الديانة التي تحقن الدم وتحفظ المال وتدخل الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take remembrance to be in the heart because Zachariah was barred from speaking; others say he could remember God aloud because only speech to people was barred, or understand the phrase as remembering God's gift and response.
rows.anchor: الذكر هنا هو بالقلب، لأنه منع من الكلام. وقيل: باللسان لأنه منع من الكلام مع الناس

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Kab al-Qurazi says that if anyone could have been excused from remembrance, it would have been Zachariah or a man in battle; the verse commands abundant remembrance so God will remember him with blessings.
rows.anchor: محمد بن كعب القرظي: لو رخص لأحد في ترك الذكر لرخص لزكريا، وللرجل في الحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kathiran is accusative either as an adjective of an omitted verbal noun or as a circumstantial accusative of the omitted verbal noun implied by udhkur, following Sibawayhi.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب: كثيرا، على أنه نعت لمصدر محذوف، أو منصوب على الحال من ضمير المصدر المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih may mean verbally declaring God free of imperfection with Subhan Allah, or prayer, as in the report that the Prophet prayed four rakas of the duha prayer.
rows.anchor: أي: نزه الله عن سمات النقص بالنطق باللسان بقولك: سبحان الله. وقيل: معنى وسبح وصل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid takes the two times literally as first light and the sun's approach to setting.
rows.anchor: أول الفجر، ووقت ميل الشمس للغروب، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view uses evening to mean the whole night and morning to mean the whole day, each part standing for its whole in a fitting metaphor.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: يحتمل أن يكون أراد بالعشي الليل، وبالإبكار النهار، فعبر بجزء كل واحد منهما عن جملته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of sabbih is omitted because it is understood from the prior command: glorify your Lord; the ba in bilashi is temporal.
rows.anchor: ومفعول: وسبح، محذوف للعلم به، لأن قبله: واذكر ربك كثيرا أي: وسبح ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A noncanonical reading al-abkar with fatḥa makes the word a plural of bakr, a time expression used adverbially for a particular day; its plural also pairs well with evening.
rows.anchor: وقرىء شاذا والأبكار، بفتح الهمزة، وهو جمع بكر بفتح الباء والكاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The canonical al-ibkar with kasra is a verbal noun, contrasted with evening as a time; it implies an omitted word such as time, and both definite nouns are generic, not confined to the three days.
rows.anchor: على قراءة الجمهور: والإبكار، بكسر الهمزة، فهو مصدر، فيكون قد قابل العشي الذي هو وقت، بالمصدر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says tasbih here means worship throughout the days, not only at the two edges of the day.
rows.anchor: الراغب: لم يعن التسبيح طرفي النهار فقط، بل إدامة العبادة في هذه الأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes tasbih as prayer: remember God through all the days and nights, and pray at the two ends of the day.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: يدل على أن المراد بالتسبيح الصلاة، ذكره العشي والإبكار فكأنه قال: اذكر ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bilashi most properly attaches to sabbih, applying the later verb in a sequence; attaching it to remember would require ellipsis, though some allow that in limited usage, or remembrance may be unbounded by these times.
rows.anchor: ويتعلق: بالعشي، بقوله: وسبح، ويكون على إعمال الثاني وهو الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage's rhetorical features include augmented form in hunalika, repetition, paired questions and answers, grammatical gender by form, a good offspring phrase, and metaphorical attribution of old age reaching Zachariah; rhetoricians prize sound patterning and ellipsis.
rows.anchor: الزيادة في البناء في قوله: هنالك، وقد ذكرت فائدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalam is the familiar writing implement, plural aqlam, and also an arrow used for drawing lots; it is linked to trimming or sharpening, or alternatively to qalamah, a thin plant and a nail clipping, with the verb meaning to pare and smooth nails.
rows.anchor: القلم: معروف وهو الذي يكتب به، وجمعه أقلام ويقع على السهم الذي يقترع به

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's line about a lion whose claws have not been trimmed illustrates the sense of qalam as cutting or paring.
rows.anchor: زهير: لدى أسد شاكي السلاح مقذف ... له لبد أظفاره لم تقلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A later poet compares the crescent to a nail clipping, illustrating qalamah as what falls when a nail is pared.
rows.anchor: يشبه بالهلال وذاك نقص ... قلامة ظفره شبه الهلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy is secretly conveying a meaning into the mind; it may come by angel to a messenger, by inspiration as with the bee, by gesture, or through writing, as in Zuhayr's line about verses preserved like revelation in stone.
rows.anchor: الوحي: إلقاء المعنى في النفس في خفاء، فقد يكون بالملك للرسل وبالإلهام كقوله: وأوحى ربك إلى النحل
